newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa updates cargo computers system.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa updates cargo computers system.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it has introduced a new global cargo management computer system and will phase in freight barcoding worldwide this year.
Joachim Haas, senior vice president Europe, said the new systems were part of the cargo airline's strategic re-positioning as a logistics services supplier.
The new cargo system, Mosaic, manages cargo bookings, airway bills and freight handling at 250 stations around the world, Haas said in a Reuters interview.
"With Mosaic we have replaced single systems which we had such as in the (Frankfurt) Lufthansa Cargo Center, the U.S. and England," he said.
From April 1, Lufthansa Cargo will start to phase in barcoding on all shipments and aims to complete the process by the end of 1997.
Haas said: "The introduction of barcoding has absolute priority. It will be for all shipments, not just express."
Barcoding would allow better tracking and tracing of freight, and was demanded by forwarders who were updating their technology, he added.
"Barcoding has advantages in rationalising, gathering of information, and is the pre-condition for our business. If every supermarket has it, then why should we not have it?" Haas said.
Introduction of barcode labels had been delayed due to difficulties in agreeing an International Air Transport Association (IATA)standard, he added.

Haas said Lufthansa would also use the change to switch its handling from a shipment basis to a piece of freight since the airline had realised its freight structure was similar to that of integrators.
"Before, we were shipment-orientated. But it makes no sense when you know about 50 percent of all pieces of freight are in the region of up to 25kg," he explained.
About 70 percent of all freight, in turn, was up to 50kg in weight, he added.
This change would also allow more automatisation of cargo handling, he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
